title: Indicators; Entropy; Gibbs free energy and feasibility; ΔG, K and Q; Electrolysis (molten and aqueous)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB08#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB08#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB08#t2 term and clue written for the game; AB08#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB08#N.3b, EN08#N.4, EN09#N.5, EN10#N.3b, RX07#N.2, AB08#N.7b, EN08#N.5b, EN09#N.8b, EN10#N.6b, RX07#N.4, AB08#N.8, EN08#N.7b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: End point
items.clue: The stage of a titration at which the indicator visibly changes.

items.label: Phenolphthalein
items.clue: A weak acid, HInd, whose Ind⁻ form is pink; it changes at about pH 8–10.

items.label: Equivalence point
items.clue: The stage at which acid and base have reacted in the stoichiometric ratio.

items.label: Universal indicator
items.clue: A mixture of several weak acids with different pKa values, used to estimate pH.

questions.stem: Acetic acid, CH₃COOH, has a pKa of 4.74. A solution of acetic acid is adjusted to a pH of 6.00 at 25°C by adding NaOH(aq). Which species, CH₃COOH or CH₃COO⁻, is present at the higher concentration in the final solution, and why?

options.text: CH₃COOH, because the pH is higher than the pKa of acetic acid
CH₃COOH, because the pH of the solution is less than 7
CH₃COO⁻, because the pH is greater than the pKa of acetic acid
Neither; the two are equal because the solution is at equilibrium

questions.explanation: Above the pKa the deprotonated form predominates: [CH₃COO⁻]/[CH₃COOH] = (1.8 × 10⁻⁵)/(1.0 × 10⁻⁶) = 18.

questions.stem: Which change has a negative entropy change, ΔS, for the system?

options.text: H₂O(l) → H₂O(g)
2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g)
C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g)
NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)

questions.explanation: Two moles of gas become one, so there are fewer ways to arrange the particles and their energy: ΔS is negative.

questions.stem: For C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g), calculate ΔG at 298 K. ΔH° = −136 kJ/mol_rxn and ΔS° = −120.7 J/(mol_rxn·K). Answers in kJ/mol_rxn.
For a certain reaction, ΔG° = −4.0 kJ/mol_rxn at 298 K. At 298 K, RT = 2.5 kJ/mol. Which statement about the value of the equilibrium constant, K, at 298 K is correct?

options.text: K is smaller than 1
K is between 1 and 10
K is between 10 and 100
K is larger than 100

questions.explanation: K = e^(4.0/2.5) = e^1.6. Since e¹ ≈ 2.7 and e² ≈ 7.4, K ≈ 5: products favored, but not by a large factor.

questions.stem: At 25°C, a reaction has ΔG° = +120 kJ/mol_rxn, and when its reactants are mixed in the laboratory almost no product forms. Which statement about obtaining a useful amount of product at 25°C, without coupling the reaction to any other reaction, is correct?

options.text: Energy must be supplied from an external source for as long as product is forming
No method can produce a useful amount of the product, because the reaction's ΔG° is positive
Adding a suitable catalyst will give a useful amount, because it lowers the activation energy
Heating the mixture briefly will start the reaction, which then continues by itself at 25°C

questions.stem: A student will titrate a solution of a weak acid, HA, with NaOH(aq) at 25°C and must choose an acid-base indicator from several whose pKa values are known. Which value should the student compare with the pKa values of the indicators in order to choose the indicator that gives the most accurate result?

options.text: The pH of the mixture at the equivalence point
The pKa of the weak acid that is being titrated
The pH of the mixture once excess NaOH is added
The pH of pure water at the same temperature

questions.explanation: An indicator's color change is centered near its pKa, so the one whose pKa is closest to the equivalence-point pH changes color as equivalence is reached.

questions.stem: A sample of neon gas in a sealed, rigid container is heated from 300 K to 600 K. According to kinetic molecular theory, which change in the neon atoms accounts for the increase in the entropy of the gas?

options.text: The kinetic energies of the atoms are spread over a wider range of values
The atoms expand and take up a larger share of the container's volume
The kinetic energies of the atoms all rise to the same, higher value
The number of atoms with the most probable kinetic energy grows larger

questions.explanation: The distribution of kinetic energy broadens as temperature increases, so energy is dispersed over a wider range of values: higher entropy.

questions.stem: For a hypothetical reaction, ΔH° = +40.0 kJ/mol_rxn and ΔS° = −50.0 J/(mol_rxn·K) at 298 K, and these values change little with temperature. A student predicts that heating the reaction mixture to 1000 K will make the reaction thermodynamically favored. Which evaluation of the prediction is correct?

options.text: It is right: at a high temperature the TΔS° term dominates, so ΔG° becomes negative
It is right: heating makes the reaction go faster, so it becomes more favored
It is wrong: ΔG° stays positive at every temperature, as ΔH° > 0 and ΔS° < 0
It is wrong: with ΔS° < 0 the reaction is favored only at low temperatures, so cool it

questions.stem: A mixture of H₂(g) and O₂(g) can be kept in a sealed container at 25°C for years with no detectable formation of water. For the reaction 2 H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2 H₂O(l), ΔG° = −474 kJ/mol_rxn at 25°C. Which statement best explains why no water is detected?

options.text: Very few H₂–O₂ collisions have enough energy to react, so water forms too slowly to detect
H₂O molecules form and decompose at equal rates, so the amounts of H₂ and O₂ remain constant
H₂ and O₂ molecules in a gas are too far apart to collide, so the reaction has no way to start
A spark is needed to supply energy, so the reaction is favored only after it has been sparked

questions.stem: A cell contains a Cu electrode in Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) and a Ni electrode in Ni(NO₃)₂(aq), joined by a salt bridge and by wires. While the cell operates, the reaction Cu(s) + Ni²⁺(aq) → Cu²⁺(aq) + Ni(s) occurs; this reaction is thermodynamically unfavored. Which classification of the cell, with its justification, is correct?

options.text: Galvanic, because it has two different metal electrodes joined by a salt bridge
Galvanic, because electrons flow through the wires from one electrode to the other
Electrolytic, because both of its half-cells contain solutions of dissolved electrolytes
Electrolytic, because the unfavored reaction is driven by an outside power supply

questions.stem: 25.0 mL of 0.100 M NH₃ is titrated with 0.100 M HCl. Which indicator is the most suitable? Ranges (each centered near the indicator's pKa): methyl orange 3.1–4.4; phenolphthalein 8.3–10.0; thymol blue 8.0–9.6; alizarin yellow 10.1–12.0.

options.text: phenolphthalein
methyl orange
thymol blue
alizarin yellow

questions.explanation: Strong acid + weak base: NH₄⁺ makes the equivalence point acidic (about pH 5.3), and the steep section runs down to about pH 3.5. Methyl orange changes there.

questions.stem: At 298 K the standard molar entropies of H₂(g), O₂(g) and H₂O(l) are 130.7, 205.2 and 70.0 J/(mol·K). A student uses these values to calculate ΔS° for the reaction 2 H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2 H₂O(l) and reports +326.6 J/(mol_rxn·K). Which evaluation of the student's result is correct?

options.text: It is right: the reaction releases much energy, so the products gain entropy
It is right: H₂O molecules contain more atoms than H₂ or O₂ molecules
It is wrong: here 3 mol of gas become 2 mol of liquid, so ΔS° is negative
It is wrong: each S° value is used only once, so ΔS° = −265.9 J/(mol_rxn·K)

questions.explanation: The correct value is 140.0 − 466.6 = −326.6 J/(mol_rxn·K); the student subtracted in the wrong order.
